title: us supreme court blocks republican drawn congressional map missouri 2026 09 10
text:
Sept 10 (Reuters) - The U.S. Supreme Court blocked Missouri on Thursday from using a redrawn congressional map that favors Republicans in November's midterm elections, dealing a setback to President Donald ​Trump and the party's odds of maintaining its slim majority in ​the House of Representatives.
The justices granted an emergency request by the map's ⁠challengers to suspend a federal judge's decision that allowed only the reconfigured boundaries ​to be used in the November 3 elections.
The court's brief order was unsigned ​and gave no explanation, as is common when the justices handle emergency matters. No justice publicly dissented from the decision.
The challengers, including a group opposed to the Republican-drawn map ​called People Not Politicians, had swiftly sought the Supreme Court's intervention ​after St. Louis, Missouri-based Chief U.S. District Judge Stephen Clark issued his decision on Tuesday.
‌Clark's ⁠decision came shortly after the Supreme Court had declined to intervene in a separate bid by Missouri officials to reinstate the redrawn map, which the state's top court had blocked until it is put to a referendum.
The ​judge's order appeared ​to conflict with ⁠the Missouri Supreme Court's unanimous September 3 ruling blocking the map, leaving the state's congressional districts in limbo and ​injecting further confusion into the high-stakes electoral fight.
Missouri Republicans ​adopted ⁠the new map, which dismantled the Kansas City-based seat of longtime Democratic Representative Emanuel Cleaver, in 2025 as part of a broader effort backed by President ⁠Donald ​Trump to redraw congressional districts in ways that ​could benefit Republican candidates.
Republicans hold a narrow 219-214 majority in the U.S. House, including ​one independent who caucuses with Republicans.
